We formalize per-batch dispatch as a fixed-charge makespan problem---NP-hard on two fully replicated GPUs, polynomial in degenerate limits---and present TEMPO, a makespan-aware dispatcher solving it in milliseconds off the critical path; its SGLang integration runs out-of-process and fuses dispatch with count collection into one in-graph kernel. End-to-end on Testbed B, Qwen3-235B (inside the win region) gains $4$--$6\%$ throughput and cuts p99 latency by $\sim 15.6\%$; DeepSeek-V3 (outside, communication-dominated) shows only mechanism cost. A phase diagram, not a universal win, is the claim: it predicts both outcomes before deployment.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: SCOPE: Subspace Clustering with Online Per-Head Top-K Estimation for Sparse Video Attention
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) incur quadratic self-attention cost over spatiotemporal tokens. Existing training-free sparse attention methods often construct sparse masks from block-level or cluster-level proxy scores, which can obscure fine-grained differences among keys and miss high contribution keys under aggressive sparsity. Moreover, such proxy scores may yield overly concentrated softmax distributions, causing Top-$p$ to retain too few keys for some query clusters. Although a fixed Top-$k$ minimum alleviates this failure mode, a shared value cannot adapt to variations across heads and inputs. To address both limitations, we propose SCOPE, a training-free sparse attention framework that combines 3D-RoPE-aligned key subspace clustering with online per-head Top-$k$ estimation for efficient video-DiT inference. SCOPE partitions post-RoPE keys into temporal, height, and width subspaces, clusters them independently, and aggregates the corresponding centroid scores through lookup tables to obtain per key proxy scores for each query cluster. Building on existing hybrid Top-$p$/fixed Top-$k$ selection, SCOPE derives a head-specific Top-$k$ value online by averaging the initial retained key counts within each head, weighted by query cluster size, and selects additional keys only for query clusters whose initial retained key counts fall below this value. Sparse attention is then computed over the selected original keys and values. Across six model--task configurations, SCOPE consistently outperforms existing training-free baselines in both fidelity and latency, achieving up to a $1.99\times$ end-to-end speedup on 720p HunyuanVideo with $28.46$ dB PSNR relative to dense attention.

In this paper, we present SliceScheduler, a dynamic operator-level scheduling system for multi-tenant model serving. The key idea is to expose cluster-wide operator execution state and enable what-if reasoning over scheduling decisions. SliceScheduler consists of four key components. First, we introduce the Global Mapping Graph (GMG), a unified abstraction that captures operator dependencies, tensor shapes, resource mappings, and execution states, providing a real-time, cluster-wide view with explicit resource semantics. Second, we build a global simulator on top of GMG to predict operator-level execution and memory evolution under candidate placements. Third, we design an incremental, simulation-based scheduling module that selects placements to exploit fragmented idle slices while avoiding memory violations and preserving SLA. Finally, we develop an operator executor that materializes scheduling decisions on GPUs and coordinates computation and cross-accelerator transfers. We implement SliceScheduler as a PyTorch backend and evaluate it using production trace replay. Experimental results show that SliceScheduler improves token throughput by 1.10--2.29$\times$ compared to existing approaches, while maintaining SLA violations within 9\%. SliceScheduler demonstrates that operator-level scheduling is a practical and effective approach to improving GPU utilization for multi-tenant LLM serving.

This discrepancy stems from the non-uniform propagation and accumulation of errors along the denoising trajectory. To address this, we propose Global-Impact Cache (GCache). We first establish a rigorous theoretical characterization of the error propagation upper bound. Recognizing that this bound can be overly conservative for complex, highly non-convex diffusion models, we further reparameterize the propagation exponent with a Bernstein form and reformulate cache policy search as a bilevel optimization problem. In detail, GCache identifies an optimal reuse policy in the inner objective while aligning the error-weighting function with generation quality loss in the outer objective. This framework effectively reconciles theoretical rigor with empirical performance, learning to prioritize computation where it most impacts visual fidelity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GCache consistently outperforms prior caching strategies on both video and image generation. Notably, on the state-of-the-art Wan2.1 video diffusion model, GCache maintains a 2.17x speedup while significantly enhancing generation quality, reducing LPIPS from 0.1095 to 0.0316.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: From LLM Inference to Agentic Workloads: Characterization and Implications for Serving Systems
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Agentic applications are shifting AI serving from isolated model inference to long-running workloads in which LLMs coordinate tools, environments, and persistent state. However, the system behavior of these workloads---where latency, cost, and bottlenecks arise---remains poorly characterized, leaving serving systems to rely on assumptions built for conventional inference. We present AgentSysBench, a benchmark suite and measurement toolkit with ten representative agentic applications and unified systems-level instrumentation. Across controlled deployments and production traces, we identify six properties that distinguish agentic workloads from conventional LLM serving: (1) execution is heavyweight and stateful, with non-LLM components dominating latency in 5 of 10 applications and sandbox working-set memory peaking at 28 GB per session; (2) applications compose components with heterogeneous resource affinity---GPU-bound inference, memory-bound retrieval, CPU-bound sandboxes---whose task latencies diverge by up to 32x; (3) bottlenecks shift across requests, models, and deployments; (4) production sessions hold state idle for minutes to hours between active steps; (5) a control-plane tax---auxiliary LLM calls and context overhead from tool schemas and observations---crowds out productive compute and context; and (6) production traces from three applications reveal heavy cross-request redundancy in search queries and web fetches, exposing a large caching opportunity. Four design explorations demonstrate that these findings are actionable: task-aware serving reduces latency by 29--40%, communication-aware placement by up to 4.5x, state offloading reduces memory usage by 4.6x, and tool-result caching removes 35.2% of redundant search calls and saves 19.3% of aggregate search latency.

We present ExactMoE, an inference design that applies symmetric group-128 four-bit weight quantization only to routed experts, stores those experts in kernel-native MARLIN form in pinned host memory, and executes all selected experts through a configurable GPU-resident slot cache and fused grouped MoE kernels. The router, attention, embeddings, normalization layers, and language-model head remain in BF16. "Exact" refers to complete expert availability and an unchanged top-k routing procedure: no expert is pruned, substituted, or forced to execute on the CPU. It does not imply numerical identity with the BF16 model. On OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct, evaluated on a single NVIDIA L4, a 16-slot configuration reduces peak reserved GPU memory from 14.168 to 1.836 GiB (87.04%) while retaining 81.85% of BF16 decode throughput. A fully resident 64-slot configuration reaches 31.923 tokens/s versus 21.662 tokens/s for BF16 while reserving 4.061 GiB. Across 12,450 zero-shot multiple-choice questions, ExactMoE obtains 70.3534% normalized accuracy versus 70.8996% for BF16, retaining 99.23% of the baseline accuracy. In a matched 16-token ablation, fused grouped execution is 1.97x as fast as a sequential W4 reference. These results identify a practical memory-transfer-throughput frontier for complete-expert MoE inference.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: EcoVLA: Energy-Efficient Device-Edge Co-Inference for Vision-Language-Action Models under Real-Time Constraints
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising foundation for Embodied AI, but their high inference cost poses significant challenges for deployment in robotic systems. In practice, on-device inference is constrained by limited compute capacity and energy budgets, struggling to simultaneously satisfy real-time control and energy efficiency requirements. Alternatively, offloading the inference workload to an edge server is susceptible to fluctuations in system conditions, introducing unpredictable latency risks. Device-edge co-inference offers a promising solution, but systematic research tailored to VLA models remains scarce, particularly a unified co-inference framework that jointly addresses real-time constraints and system-level energy efficiency. Thus, we propose EcoVLA, an adaptive device-edge co-inference framework for VLA models that maximizes system energy efficiency under real-time constraints. EcoVLA first introduces a unified stage-level abstraction over different VLA paradigms, establishing an architecture-agnostic co-inference design space. It then formulates a joint device-edge-network latency and energy prediction model to enable rapid runtime evaluation of candidate co-inference schemes. Building on this, EcoVLA continuously selects the energy-optimal scheme satisfying real-time constraints with millisecond-level overhead, adapting to runtime variations in network and system states. Furthermore, EcoVLA incorporates a lightweight transmission mechanism for inter-stage intermediate tensors to reduce the communication overhead incurred by cross-device collaboration. Experimental results across VLA models show that EcoVLA improves system energy efficiency by up to 236% over existing co-inference approaches under a 20 Hz action output frequency constraint, while consistently maintaining SLO satisfaction under dynamic network and edge workload conditions.

p0_strong_or_canonical.title: Beyond Capacity: Scalable MoE LLM Inference via High-Bandwidth Flash with Direct GPU and HBM Paths
p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Modern mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models increasingly strain the capacity and cost efficiency of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), as rapidly growing expert weights must be provisioned close to GPUs. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) offers substantially greater capacity, but conventional designs typically deliver HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through HBM, leaving an additional direct GPU-HBF connection underutilized. We explore an HBF organization that simultaneously exploits two independent expert-delivery routes: a direct path that transfers expert weights from HBF to the GPU and a relay path that transfers them from HBF through the HBM base die to the GPU. Whole experts are assigned to one of the two routes, and transfers over both routes proceed concurrently, increasing aggregate expert-delivery bandwidth without replicating expert weights or introducing a shared relay bottleneck. Early expert determination identifies upcoming experts ahead of their conventional execution point, allowing HBF read latency to overlap with preceding computation, while separate management of immutable expert weights and mutable KV-cache data reduces interference between the two traffic classes. We evaluate the architecture using an event-driven continuous-batching LLM serving simulator with empirically measured GPU compute latencies. Across representative MoE workloads, concurrently utilizing the direct GPU-HBF and HBF-HBM-GPU routes consistently improves expert-delivery efficiency over designs restricted to either route alone. For a representative workload, the proposed architecture can achieve 1.94$\times$ higher throughput and 1.90$\times$ end-to-end speedup over a design that delivers all HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through the HBM base die.

p0_strong_or_canonical.why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in the field of embodied AI, but their high computational cost and limited predicted action length hinder real-time deployment. Although Dadu-Corki, a dedicated accelerator for efficient embodied AI, has been introduced, it does not exploit the inherent interaction patterns between the robot and its environment, which results in a relatively short predicted action length. We observe that robotic environments naturally alternate between active states-where precise actions are crucial-and inactive states-where actions have limited impact on task success. This insight enables a new scheduling opportunity: long-action-length speculative prediction in inactive states, paired with selective verification in active states. We propose SpecVLA, an algorithm-system co-design framework that adaptively balances action length, inference latency, and task reliability. On the algorithm side, SpecVLA introduces a state-aware VLA inference execution paradigm and a hardware-friendly construction of a smaller verification model (sVLA) using differential residuals and block-wise mixed-precision quantization. On the system side, we develop a heterogeneous architecture consisting of a GPU and a robotic-specific hardware module, along with a speculative dataflow that decouples VLA and sVLA through parallel execution. Comprehensive evaluations on OpenVLA and RDT across LIBERO and ManiSkill benchmarks show that SpecVLA reduces end-to-end latency significantly while preserving task success rate. By enabling long-action-length speculative prediction with timely verification, SpecVLA achieves real-time robotic manipulation with both high efficiency and reliability.

p1_watchlist.title: LLMRunner: Closed Workload Model Performance Testing Framework for LLM Servings
p1_watchlist.why: LLMRunner contributes realistic closed-workload, multi-turn LLM-serving performance tests with think-time, KV-cache and GPU monitoring; high-value evaluation infrastructure, although it is not itself an inference optimization.

p1_watchlist.title: Bind-WAM: Binding-Uncertainty-Guided Selective Future Imagination in World Action Models
p1_watchlist.why: Bind-WAM selectively invokes expensive future-action imagination only when language-object binding uncertainty warrants it, using a lightweight router. This directly targets WAM inference cost and is protected Physical-AI work, but the abstract does not quantify latency/FLOP savings.

p1_watchlist.title: SAVE: Less is More in Agentic Video Reasoning
p1_watchlist.why: SAVE performs controlled, token- and cost-accounted comparisons of agentic video reasoning; it finds elaborate agents often add cost without consistent gains and proposes a minimal explorer that wins five of six settings. This is valuable efficient-reasoning evidence rather than a new serving kernel.

p1_watchlist.title: SkinAdvisor: An AI-Driven Decision Framework for Skin Production Planning via Multi-Modal Transformer Sales Forecasting
p1_watchlist.why: A deployed multi-modal Transformer forecasting system with an explicit serving pipeline, single-pass decoding, p99 latency below 8 ms, and throughput above 1,100 requests/s on a 16-core CPU. High-value deployment evidence for multimodal serving, although the application is domain-specific and does not present a dedicated accelerator.

p1_watchlist.title: EvoX: Rethinking the Agent Harness as a Runtime Policy
p1_watchlist.why: EvoX provides a deterministic multi-model agent runtime with action realization, execution continuity and outcome grounding; it leads six-harness comparisons on 691 task-model pairs. High-value agent-runtime architecture, though not a direct token/latency optimization.

p1_watchlist.title: FIRE: Failure Isolation and Reliability for Production-Connected Experiments at Scale
p1_watchlist.why: Describes production-connected experimentation inside a large recommendation-serving system, with explicit capacity isolation, dependency monitoring, and traffic pinning; the reported sub-1% serving-capacity footprint makes it relevant to serving infrastructure and safe experimentation.

p1_watchlist.title: LOHRE: Execution-Grounded Type Recovery via LLM-Orchestrated Hybrid Analysis
p1_watchlist.why: Compresses execution traces for an LLM-orchestrated agent workflow and reports lower token use and runtime than full-trace feedback; retain as a concrete agent-execution efficiency result pending full-text generality and quality audit.

p1_watchlist.title: HeadIO: Body-Frame Heading Decomposition for Neural Inertial Odometry on Head-Mounted Devices
p1_watchlist.why: HeadIO improves head-mounted inertial odometry while using nearly 3x fewer FLOPs and 8x fewer parameters than the learned-equivariant baseline, with real-time wearable deployment relevance. It is a strong edge/Physical-AI efficiency watch item, outside core LLM serving.

p1_watchlist.title: Learning Low-Latency Action Verification for Frozen Vision-Language-Action Models
p1_watchlist.why: HDH uses a compact verifier trained from frozen-VLA deployment rollouts to select action chunks; the real-robot success gains make it valuable for action-head/runtime study, but the abstract does not establish a direct latency or throughput gain.

p1_watchlist.title: OverServe: Resource Amplification Attacks on SaaS Agents via Tool--Prompt Co-Design
p1_watchlist.why: OverServe 对 SaaS agents 的工具调用与停止判定进行 tool-prompt co-design，实测最多放大 API 请求 93.88 倍且原任务检查仍通过；直接揭示 agent serving 的资源放大与终止控制风险，对高效 agent runtime/harness 设计具有高价值。

p1_watchlist.title: Risk-Aware Joint Inference and Resource Control for Physical AI in 6G Networks
p1_watchlist.why: RACE couples action-failure risk to wireless reliability and edge-inference resource control for Physical AI; it is a valuable cross-layer deployment direction, though its main contribution is networking/control rather than model-kernel acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
p1_watchlist.why: The official Atom abstract provides a unified profiling dataset and benchmark for LLM training simulators across model families and NPU-cluster configurations.

p1_watchlist.title: Elastic-WAM: Adaptive Spatiotemporal Imagination for Efficient Robot Control
p1_watchlist.why: The official Atom abstract proposes action-grounded adaptive allocation of world-model refinement across denoising time and future spatial regions; retain as protected Physical-AI inference work pending full efficiency validation.

p1_watchlist.title: HiPFuse: Real-Time LiDAR Semantic Segmentation for Robotic Perception on Edge Devices
p1_watchlist.why: The official Atom abstract reports real-time LiDAR segmentation on Jetson AGX Orin at 14.2–22.4 FPS and improved downstream odometry, relevant to edge Physical-AI perception.

p1_watchlist.title: SFU-Sim: Bit-Exact Reverse Engineering of NVIDIA MUFU and Validation of PTX Paths
p1_watchlist.why: The official Atom abstract builds bit-exact models of NVIDIA MUFU/PTX paths across GPU generations, useful for architecture-level performance and correctness analysis.

p1_watchlist.title: Uncovering the Memory Hierarchy of Modern NVIDIA GPUs for Accurate Simulation
p1_watchlist.why: The official Atom abstract reverse-engineers modern NVIDIA GPU cache, routing, replacement, and interconnect behavior relevant to LLM memory-system modeling.

p1_watchlist.title: Swanada: Split-Encoder Capability-Routed Conformer CTC and Sub-30 MB On-Device Speech Recognition Across Twelve Scripts
p1_watchlist.why: The official Atom abstract describes a sub-30 MB on-device streaming ASR system across twelve scripts with quantized/runtime-aware deployment; retain for deeper systems evaluation.

p1_watchlist.title: FAME-QP: A GPU-Accelerated Quadratic-Programming Solver for Real-Time Model Predictive Control
p1_watchlist.why: The official Atom abstract presents a GPU-accelerated quadratic-program solver for real-time model-predictive control, including CUDA-graph execution and device calibration; retain as Physical-AI runtime adjacency.

p1_watchlist.title: OpticalRAG: Pixel-Space Compression for Token-Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation
p1_watchlist.topic: Pixel-space token compression for retrieval-augmented generation
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract compresses retrieved document content through a frozen visual encoder and query-conditioned distillation to as few as 16 injected tokens, while improving compression-aware accuracy on three long-context benchmarks. This is a high-value multimodal context-compression result pending full-text validation and broader serving-cost measurements.

p1_watchlist.title: Machine-learning decoders for fusion-based quantum computing in real time
p1_watchlist.why: PRISM is a transformer-based ML decoder with an optimized AMD VP1902 FPGA implementation, reporting 6.59-microsecond logical-block latency and 1.56-microsecond amortized decoding time while matching integer-programming decoder error rates. This is a concrete real-time ML inference and FPGA co-design result; retain as a high-value cross-domain accelerator watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: Benchmarking Vendor-Guided Optimizations on Edge NPUs: From NPU Only to End-to-End Performance. Extended technical report
p1_watchlist.topic: End-to-end deployment optimization across heterogeneous edge NPUs
p1_watchlist.why: This cross-platform study measures vendor-guided model and deployment optimizations across four edge NPUs and separates NPU-only from end-to-end latency. The reported additional 10.4–70.7% system-latency reduction and ranking reversals are directly useful for heterogeneous edge-AI deployment and systems evaluation; retain as a high-value engineering watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
p1_watchlist.topic: Low-bit quantization-aware distillation for LLM agents
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract directly addresses task-success degradation in low-bit LLM agents and introduces closed-loop teacher steering to repair quantized rollouts. Results across multiple agent benchmarks and models, including improved W4A16 quality and lower training GPU hours, make this a high-value quantization watchlist item pending full-text validation.

p1_watchlist.title: AdjointFlow: Accelerating Scientific Inverse Problems with Physics-Based Transport
p1_watchlist.topic: Physics-informed flow transport for faster scientific inverse-problem inference
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract embeds known physics into a stochastic-interpolant transport and reports inference up to five orders of magnitude faster than iterative plug-and-play methods. It is a strong neighboring contribution to diffusion/flow inference acceleration, although its scope is scientific inverse problems rather than image/video generation.

p1_watchlist.title: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion for Combinatorial Optimization in Multi-Robot Task Allocation
p1_watchlist.topic: Training-free discrete diffusion for multi-robot action allocation
p1_watchlist.why: The work extends model-based diffusion to discrete multi-robot task allocation without offline training and reports near-real-time optimization at a fraction of the computational cost of MIP/RL alternatives. It is a direct Physical-AI action-allocation and diffusion-inference signal, so retain as a high-value watch item even though it is algorithmic rather than a hardware accelerator.

p1_watchlist.title: One Trajectory, Two Requirements: Accuracy and Local Stability in Euler Sampling for Flow Matching Policies
p1_watchlist.topic: Flow-matching action-policy sampling and local stability for robot inference
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract directly studies inference-time Euler sampling for flow-matching robot policies, separating trajectory-accuracy requirements from local-stability requirements. It evaluates a frozen pi_0.5-LIBERO policy and reports 4–9 steps at 5% terminal error versus 87–112 at 1% on selected inputs. This is directly relevant to action-generation/flow-policy serving and merits retention, although it does not yet demonstrate a new adaptive sampler or end-to-end speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: Network-Co-Designed Dynamic Sparsification for Dependable Distributed Robot Learning over 3GPP Networks
p1_watchlist.topic: Network-co-designed dynamic sparsification for distributed robot learning
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract directly couples update sparsification to byte budgets and network timing for distributed learning across robot fleets under volatile 3GPP links. This is a protected Physical-AI communication/runtime direction; the reported communication reduction warrants a high-value watchlist and full-text validation of convergence and quantitative trade-offs.

p1_watchlist.title: GigaEdge Spench: An SDK for Practical Streaming Speech Enhancement
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract presents a practical streaming neural speech-enhancement SDK across CPU servers, mobile devices and browsers, with INT8 and FP32 models, shared model resources and ONNX Runtime/TensorFlow Lite/WebAssembly backends. Its measured real-time multi-stream deployment makes it a high-value edge/streaming-inference watchlist item pending full-text and scaling validation.

p1_watchlist.title: How Much of Your VLA Is kNN
p1_watchlist.topic: Retrieval-based action-chunk reuse as a VLA inference alternative
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract shows that nearest-demonstration retrieval and action-chunk reuse reach 91.7% LIBERO success without policy training and remain robust under perturbations across nine public VLAs. This is a high-value Physical-AI inference alternative that merits full-text review, although latency and retrieval-scaling evidence remain to be checked.

p1_watchlist.title: Catch It Where It Happens: Real Time Error Correction During LLM Reasoning
p1_watchlist.topic: Deterministic online verification to avoid wasted LLM reasoning tokens
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract validates symbolic reasoning steps with code instead of a competing verifier model, allowing the LLM to continue from the first detected error. It improves accuracy while adding only 6–7% tokens and avoiding verifier GPU use, making it a high-value efficient-reasoning watchlist item pending broader-domain validation.

p1_watchlist.title: How Far Does Second-Order Linear Response Predict Quantization Mismatch? Pre-Registered Measurements on Five Language Models

p1_watchlist.title: Phrase-Level Speculative Decoding on a Frozen Target
p1_watchlist.why: WATCHLIST_HIGH_VALUE: The first-party abstract is materially relevant to an active efficient-ML or protected Physical-AI direction, but the current evidence is narrower, benchmark-led, early-stage, or less conclusive than the strong tier; retain for follow-up rather than discard. Paper: Phrase-Level Speculative Decoding on a Frozen Target. All of them draft in the target's own vocabulary, so one node of the candidate tree is one target token, and the tokenizer makes that unit look like a constant. It is not. p1_watchlist.title: To SIMD or Not to SIMD: Comparing RVV vs. CGRA SoCs for Non-Linear Functions in AI
p1_watchlist.why: WATCHLIST_HIGH_VALUE: The first-party abstract is materially relevant to an active efficient-ML or protected Physical-AI direction, but the current evidence is narrower, benchmark-led, early-stage, or less conclusive than the strong tier; retain for follow-up rather than discard. Paper: To SIMD or Not to SIMD: Comparing RVV vs. CGRA SoCs for Non-Linear Functions in AI. Official arXiv abstract evidence: Non-linear functions are an important class of operations in modern large language models. However, chip vendors building for AI have so far relied on traditional vector or scalar processing units for non-linear functions. The performance of these units has not kept pace with matrix multiplication units (MMUs), which can be found in both high-performance and edge-computing devices from almost every vendor. p1_watchlist.title: PTC-IoU: CPU-Friendly Detection Quality Estimation for Edge Video Analytics
p1_watchlist.why: WATCHLIST_HIGH_VALUE: The first-party abstract is materially relevant to an active efficient-ML or protected Physical-AI direction, but the current evidence is narrower, benchmark-led, early-stage, or less conclusive than the strong tier; retain for follow-up rather than discard. Paper: PTC-IoU: CPU-Friendly Detection Quality Estimation for Edge Video Analytics. Official arXiv abstract evidence: An edge video analytics system must estimate the quality of local detections since there are no ground-truth labels available during runtime. Detectors usually provide confidence scores for their results, but these scores can not reveal every missed object or misplaced bounding box. So a quality estimator is necessary to provide a decision signal indicating which frame has potential detection failures that need to be escalated to a more powerful model in the cloud. p1_watchlist.title: Mitigating SM-Level Load Imbalance in 3D Gaussian Splatting on GPUs
p1_watchlist.why: WATCHLIST_HIGH_VALUE: The first-party abstract is materially relevant to an active efficient-ML or protected Physical-AI direction, but the current evidence is narrower, benchmark-led, early-stage, or less conclusive than the strong tier; retain for follow-up rather than discard. Paper: Mitigating SM-Level Load Imbalance in 3D Gaussian Splatting on GPUs. However, existing optimizations rely on algorithmic changes that often require retraining, or on specialized accelerators that lack flexibility across evolving 3DGS variants. p1_watchlist.title: ForgeSystem: An Architecture for Demand-Specific Artefact Production with AI Agents
p1_watchlist.why: WATCHLIST_HIGH_VALUE: The first-party abstract is materially relevant to an active efficient-ML or protected Physical-AI direction, but the current evidence is narrower, benchmark-led, early-stage, or less conclusive than the strong tier; retain for follow-up rather than discard. Paper: ForgeSystem: An Architecture for Demand-Specific Artefact Production with AI Agents. Official arXiv abstract evidence: General-purpose software serves many different demands, but this flexibility costs performance and efficiency on any specific demand. Software tailored to a specific demand avoids these losses, yet developing it requires substantial time and effort from human experts. AI agents offer an alternative: they can design, implement and test artefacts tailored to individual demands. We call this production paradigm Forge. p1_watchlist.title: Toward Sustainable Agentic AI: Carbon Tradeoffs Across Iterative Self-Refinement and Tool-Augmented Coding
p1_watchlist.why: The paper measures energy/carbon trade-offs of iterative refinement and tool-augmented coding agents, including the cost of extra reasoning steps and resolved-task-normalized efficiency; the estimates omit prompt tokens and tool execution, so it is a useful but incomplete agent-efficiency study.

p1_watchlist.title: Real-Time Volumetric Light Transport Inference without a Path
p1_watchlist.why: The paper uses an attention-augmented image-to-image network for real-time volumetric light-transport inference from inexpensive scene features, replacing costly path-traced estimates; it is a strong learned-rendering efficiency case study.

p1_watchlist.title: TSFFormer: A Frequency-Domain Spike Transformer for Green Human Activity Recognition
p1_watchlist.why: TSFFormer uses Fourier-domain mixing to reduce attention complexity and reports faster training across eight wearable benchmarks with a very low claimed energy footprint. Retain pending independent hardware-energy validation.

p1_watchlist.title: MIRIX-2.0: Multi-Agent Memory System
p1_watchlist.topic: Efficient agent systems / persistent multi-agent memory
p1_watchlist.why: MIRIX-2.0 uses typed memory agents, provenance indexing and explicit retrieval budgets, with competitive QA and procedural-memory results and faster answers than HyperMem in timed benchmarks. Retain as an agent-memory systems lead pending more direct resource/latency quantification.

p1_watchlist.title: Four-Step Text-Bearing Image Generation via Distillation with Local Response Regularization and Teacher-Guided Training
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract describes four-step DiT distillation with local-response regularization and teacher-guided text supervision, reporting 1.742 s versus 5.818 s teacher inference (3.34x) at the same 40 GB memory requirement and improved text accuracy. This is a direct image-generation acceleration contribution; retain for full-paper review of quality, baseline fairness, and generalization beyond the reported settings.

p1_watchlist.title: HIST3R: Decomposing and Rectifying State Updates with History for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract introduces history-guided direction and magnitude correction for recurrent streaming 3D reconstruction while retaining CUT3R memory footprint and inference speed, and reports sizable long-horizon pose/reconstruction improvements. This is relevant to streaming world models, bounded-memory runtime, and Physical AI; retain for deeper review of temporal robustness and end-to-end deployment.

p1_watchlist.title: HyPLM Technical Report
p1_watchlist.topic: Protein language models / efficient training and inference engine
p1_watchlist.why: HyPLM-Flash reports 130,000 residues/s on one H20 and 1.9x-2.7x faster inference than other 600M-class encoders at competitive accuracy, with released weights and engine. Retain as a high-value domain-specific efficiency result.

p1_watchlist.title: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract introduces a long-horizon AI-infrastructure optimization benchmark with 150 runs and over 10,000 GPU-hours, and reports an agent-discovered KV-cache compression improvement over a human-designed baseline. This is highly relevant to efficient agent systems, KV-cache optimization, and runtime/infra operations; retain for careful review of task validity, reproducibility, and model/tool attribution.

p1_watchlist.title: Can LLM Agents Organize Their Own Memory?
p1_watchlist.why: SoMem lets agents organize persistent memory into linked documents and retrieve evidence-backed compact contexts across long-term tasks; it is highly relevant to agent memory/runtime systems, though token and latency savings are not quantified in the abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: LO-World: Unified BEV Latent Modeling for Joint 4D Occupancy and LiDAR Forecasting
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract presents a joint 4D occupancy/LiDAR world model with a flow-matching generator that caches historical context to reduce iterative sampling latency; it reports over 25 FPS on one RTX 4090 and measurable forecasting gains. This is directly relevant to world-model efficiency and Physical AI, but the full paper should validate the cache ablation, latency methodology, and embodied deployment evidence.

p1_watchlist.title: Adaptive Entropy-Sparing for Efficient Reasoning
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract proposes selective entropy-based control of reasoning length and reports up to 52.9% shorter reasoning with up to 3.8% higher mean accuracy across eight benchmarks. This is directly relevant to efficient reasoning and inference-token reduction; retain for deeper review of training overhead, evaluation protocol, and robustness across model families.

p1_watchlist.title: How Many Candidates Does a One-Step World Model Need? A Random-Codebook Account of Nearest-of-m Training on Frozen DINO Tokens
p1_watchlist.why: The official abstract compares one-step stochastic world-model generation with multi-step flow matching and reports better enumerated-future coverage at roughly 1/30 of the 50-step flow-matching latency, plus a one-third long-horizon error reduction on Push-T. It is directly relevant to flow/action-generation efficiency and Physical AI, but its negative planning-success result and real-robot generalization limits require full-paper scrutiny.

p1_watchlist.title: DeltaForge: A Post-hoc Mixture-of-Experts VLA for Multi-Domain Autonomous Driving
p1_watchlist.topic: Physical AI / multi-domain driving VLA mixture-of-experts
p1_watchlist.why: DeltaForge consolidates independently fine-tuned driving VLA experts using shared low-rank structure and lightweight routers, approaching per-domain expert accuracy at close to single-model parameter and compute cost. Retain as a high-value efficient VLA specialization lead.

p1_watchlist.title: ACROSSVAM3.0: Resource-Bounded 4D Scene Construction and Adaptive Surface Association
p1_watchlist.why: ACROSSVAM3.0 is a resource-bounded single-GPU 4D scene-construction pipeline combining video generation, dynamic reconstruction, and SLAM with a measured 17.14 GB process-tree footprint; it is relevant to 3D/video generation infrastructure, although it does not yet demonstrate a clear speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: Why Kubernetes Cannot Contain a Full Lazy-Pulling Cache: Two Impossibility Results and a Bounded, Honest Design for Model Serving
p1_watchlist.why: The work identifies concrete Kubernetes model-serving cache failure modes and provides an owner-controlled byte-bounded cache that reads 150.3GB with zero errors in tested campaigns. Retain as a high-value serving-infrastructure reliability lead; its main result is correctness and boundedness rather than inference speed.

p1_watchlist.title: Accelerated Reinforcement Learning for Soft Robotics: Hours Instead of Years
p1_watchlist.why: The soft-robotics study replaces expensive RNN/Transformer-based policy training with a 6,924-parameter reduced-order model, achieving a three-hour training run where hardware interaction would extrapolate to years; it is a compelling Physical-AI training-efficiency result with hardware deployment.

p1_watchlist.title: Autonomous Continual Learning and Knowledge Transfer via Cortex-Inspired Neural Assemblies
p1_watchlist.why: Functional Task Networks use sparse binary inference-time routing over partially trained subnetworks for continual learning and knowledge transfer, making it relevant to sparse/MoE-style model execution, although direct latency or energy measurements are not reported.

p1_watchlist.title: Streaming Failure Forecasting: VLA Failure Monitors That Keep Learning After Deployment
p1_watchlist.topic: Physical AI / streaming VLA failure monitoring
p1_watchlist.why: SFF adapts a VLA failure monitor online by refitting only its readout at 2.18 ms per policy call and improves failure ranking under unannounced task/policy drift across real robot runs. Retain as a high-value runtime-safety/monitoring component.

p1_watchlist.title: UTOPI: Efficient Egocentric Long-Video Understanding in AR via User-Guided Token Pre-Compression
p1_watchlist.topic: Multimodal long-video inference / AR token pre-compression
p1_watchlist.why: UTOPI uses viewpoint overlap and eye-tracking to prune egocentric video before model inference, reporting up to 95% compression while preserving benchmark performance. Retain as a high-value multimodal/edge token-reduction method.

p1_watchlist.title: Kimodo-Policy: Learning Kinematic Action Models for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
p1_watchlist.why: Kimodo-Policy uses a pretrained motion generator as the action-generation backbone for humanoid loco-manipulation, with 678M parameters (92M trainable), 72.14% HumanoidArena success, and 60% mean success over eight real-world tasks. This is a high-value WAM/action-generation lead, but the abstract does not report inference latency, throughput, or energy; retain as P1 and attempt the primary arXiv PDF.

p1_watchlist.title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
p1_watchlist.why: The paper studies execution-memory evolution for embodied MLLM agents and reports substantial token reduction while retaining RoboDojo performance; it is a promising agent-runtime efficiency result, though not a serving-hardware contribution.

p1_watchlist.title: ForeAct: Geometry-Guided Action Learning from World Representations
p1_watchlist.topic: Physical AI / single-pass world-model representation for action generation
p1_watchlist.why: ForeAct removes iterative future-frame synthesis and denoising by reusing a video world model as a single-pass representation backbone for low-latency robot control, with strong simulation and real-world success. Retain as a high-value action-generation lead pending explicit latency/compute comparisons.

p1_watchlist.title: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM post-training / quantized asynchronous rollout systems
p1_watchlist.why: The study quantifies training-inference mismatch in on-policy distillation and shows FP8 plus asynchronous rollouts can provide 1.93x KV-token capacity and 1.62x faster training at preserved quality. Retain as a high-value training/serving co-design result.

p1_watchlist.title: Unlearning at Speed: Rapid Activation Dampening for Efficient Machine Unlearning in Real-World Face Recognition
p1_watchlist.why: Rapid Activation Dampening targets machine unlearning in large-scale open-set face-recognition models by identifying and suppressing identity-associated neurons. The abstract reports strong forgetting with preserved utility and substantially faster unlearning across recent architectures; this is a direct model-update efficiency lead, but detailed time/compute measurements and trade-offs need paper-level verification. Retain as P1 and attempt the primary arXiv PDF.

p1_watchlist.title: Beyond Similarity Entropy: A Rank-Guided Data-Free Quantization Framework for Vision Transformers
p1_watchlist.topic: Vision Transformer deployment / data-free low-bit quantization
p1_watchlist.why: RankQ-ViT targets mobile ViT deployment with data-free calibration and block-wise low-bit reconstruction, a direct quantization direction. Retain pending stronger quantified accuracy, latency and memory comparisons.

p1_watchlist.title: EbbFlow: PINN-Inspired Progressive Curriculum for MeanFlow Training
p1_watchlist.why: EbbFlow changes the training-time temporal supervision schedule for MeanFlow and improves FID at one- and two-network-evaluation sampling settings on ImageNet 256x256. This is a direct few-step flow-generation lead, but its inference procedure is unchanged and the abstract notes protocol-dependent benefits; retain as P1 and attempt the primary PDF.

p1_watchlist.title: Dhara: Evidence-Oriented Retrieval for Indian Knowledge Systems
p1_watchlist.why: Dhara provides measured neural-retrieval latency and storage comparisons, with BGE-M3 substantially faster than ColBERTv2 under matched hardware while retaining competitive evidence retrieval; it is a useful retrieval-serving efficiency case study, though domain-specific.

p1_watchlist.title: Graphene: A Lightweight Transformer with Ising Mean-Field Refinement for Image Super-Resolution
p1_watchlist.why: Graphene reports substantial parameter, FLOP, latency and memory reductions on image super-resolution while improving PSNR. Retain as a high-value compact-vision architecture, pending broader deployment and workload evidence.

p1_watchlist.title: Control-Aware Command Generation for Asynchronous Control and Action Inference with Vision-Based Policies towards Fast Execution
p1_watchlist.topic: Physical AI / asynchronous VLA control and action inference
p1_watchlist.why: The framework combines asynchronous policy inference, tracking control and variance-based action skipping on real bimanual robots. It is directly relevant to fast action execution, but the abstract does not quantify the speedup or provide a detailed latency/energy breakdown.

p1_watchlist.title: When Calibration Data Matter in Sub-4-Bit Language Model Quantization
p1_watchlist.why: FragCal-DC studies calibration data at 2-4 bits across dense models up to 70B and reports a 1.83-point mean accuracy gain for two-bit SignRound V2. It is directly relevant quantization evidence, but the main contribution is calibration quality rather than an inference-system or hardware advance.

p1_watchlist.title: PRISM: Preference-based Reward and Uncertainty-Integrated Synthesis Minimization for RTL PPA Optimization
p1_watchlist.why: PRISM uses LLM-generated RTL rewrites, equivalence filtering, reward modeling, and uncertainty-aware selection to improve PPA under limited commercial synthesis calls across several technology nodes; it is highly relevant to accelerator/RTL design automation, though the abstract omits quantitative PPA gains.

p1_watchlist.title: When Is High-Bandwidth Flash Cost-Effective for LLM Inference?
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM inference infrastructure / high-bandwidth flash and GPU capacity economics
p1_watchlist.why: The study evaluates HBF integration across nine dense/MoE models and multiple GPU scales, finding substantial capacity and offline-throughput benefits in specific regimes. Retain for hardware-memory-system relevance, while noting that the evidence is simulation/component-data based.

p1_watchlist.title: Elastic Representations via Hyperbolic Geometry
p1_watchlist.why: HERL provides post-hoc dimension-adaptive embedding compression and expansion through a lightweight adaptor without retraining the base encoder, preserving downstream performance across image and text modalities at a fraction of the computational cost. tracking_records.why: Long-context prefill in large language models (LLMs) incurs substantial computation and memory traffic because dense self-attention computes quadratic query-key scores. Existing methods either use a uniform low-precision path or select token interactions, leaving spatial precision routing over hardware-aligned score tiles outside fused dense attention. We introduce TileMix, a tile-centric precision-routing kernel that makes numerical precision an executable spatial decision over score-tile groups within fused dense attention. TileMix partitions the attention matrix into hardware-aligned score tiles, packs routing decisions into compact bitmasks, and dispatches each tile group through FP16 or INT8 score computation while both paths update a shared online-softmax state. Scalable precision grouping lets each routing bit govern multiple adjacent key tiles, preserving hardware-aligned compute tiles and compact metadata at long contexts. By routing all legal tile groups, TileMix preserves dense token connectivity, requires no training, and supports grouped-query attention, variable-length batches, and INT8 key/value caches. Across LongEval, LV-Eval, and A100 prefill benchmarks on LLaMA, Qwen, and Vicuna, TileMix recovers long-context quality lost under uniform INT8 and improves prefill throughput over FP16, yielding a controllable accuracy-efficiency frontier across model families. The implementation is available at https://github.com/HanzhiZhang-Ulrica/TileMix.

tracking_records.why: In expert-parallel (EP) MoE serving, every layer synchronizes at the slowest GPU. Dispatchers balance token counts (EPLB, LPLB, UltraEP) or activated-expert counts (METRO), assuming expert time is linear in one. Measurements on two datacenter GPU generations show it is neither: below $n^* \approx 156$--$168$ tokens, HBM weight streaming dominates---cost attaches to $activated replicas$, not tokens; above it, grouped GEMM rounds tokens to 128-tile $M$-tiles, so $splitting$ an expert adds padded compute. A max-affine profile $t=\max(a+bG,\,c+βN)$ captures both regimes. Realistic decode batches hold hot experts in the linear regime and cold in the flat $simultaneously$; recorded batches show proxy dispatches differ by $1.4$--$1.6\times$ in modeled block time (p95 up to $1.7\times$), and $which$ proxy wins flips with the regime. We formalize per-batch dispatch as a fixed-charge makespan problem---NP-hard on two fully replicated GPUs, polynomial in degenerate limits---and present TEMPO, a makespan-aware dispatcher solving it in milliseconds off the critical path; its SGLang integration runs out-of-process and fuses dispatch with count collection into one in-graph kernel. Anchored by an 8-GPU Testbed A microbenchmark, TEMPO stays within $1\%$ of the best fixed baseline everywhere and wins by up to $15.5\%$ where regimes mix. End-to-end on Testbed B, Qwen3-235B (inside the win region) gains $4$--$6\%$ throughput and cuts p99 latency by $\sim 15.6\%$; DeepSeek-V3 (outside, communication-dominated) shows only mechanism cost. A phase diagram, not a universal win, is the claim: it predicts both outcomes before deployment.

tracking_records.title: SCOPE: Subspace Clustering with Online Per-Head Top-K Estimation for Sparse Video Attention
tracking_records.why: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) incur quadratic self-attention cost over spatiotemporal tokens. Existing training-free sparse attention methods often construct sparse masks from block-level or cluster-level proxy scores, which can obscure fine-grained differences among keys and miss high contribution keys under aggressive sparsity. Moreover, such proxy scores may yield overly concentrated softmax distributions, causing Top-$p$ to retain too few keys for some query clusters. Although a fixed Top-$k$ minimum alleviates this failure mode, a shared value cannot adapt to variations across heads and inputs. To address both limitations, we propose SCOPE, a training-free sparse attention framework that combines 3D-RoPE-aligned key subspace clustering with online per-head Top-$k$ estimation for efficient video-DiT inference. SCOPE partitions post-RoPE keys into temporal, height, and width subspaces, clusters them independently, and aggregates the corresponding centroid scores through lookup tables to obtain per key proxy scores for each query cluster. Building on existing hybrid Top-$p$/fixed Top-$k$ selection, SCOPE derives a head-specific Top-$k$ value online by averaging the initial retained key counts within each head, weighted by query cluster size, and selects additional keys only for query clusters whose initial retained key counts fall below this value. Sparse attention is then computed over the selected original keys and values. Across six model--task configurations, SCOPE consistently outperforms existing training-free baselines in both fidelity and latency, achieving up to a $1.99\times$ end-to-end speedup on 720p HunyuanVideo with $28.46$ dB PSNR relative to dense attention.

tracking_records.title: Global Simulation-Guided Dynamic Operator Scheduling for Efficient Multi-Tenant Model Serving
tracking_records.why: Container-granularity scheduling leaves abundant short-lived idle slices within containers unexploited. Reallocating containers is too heavyweight to utilize such fine-grained opportunities under SLA constraints, and operator-level scheduling requires reasoning about dependencies, memory safety, and cluster-wide execution dynamics in real time. In this paper, we present SliceScheduler, a dynamic operator-level scheduling system for multi-tenant model serving. The key idea is to expose cluster-wide operator execution state and enable what-if reasoning over scheduling decisions. SliceScheduler consists of four key components. First, we introduce the Global Mapping Graph (GMG), a unified abstraction that captures operator dependencies, tensor shapes, resource mappings, and execution states, providing a real-time, cluster-wide view with explicit resource semantics. Second, we build a global simulator on top of GMG to predict operator-level execution and memory evolution under candidate placements. Third, we design an incremental, simulation-based scheduling module that selects placements to exploit fragmented idle slices while avoiding memory violations and preserving SLA. Finally, we develop an operator executor that materializes scheduling decisions on GPUs and coordinates computation and cross-accelerator transfers. We implement SliceScheduler as a PyTorch backend and evaluate it using production trace replay. Experimental results show that SliceScheduler improves token throughput by 1.10--2.29$\times$ compared to existing approaches, while maintaining SLA violations within 9\%. SliceScheduler demonstrates that operator-level scheduling is a practical and effective approach to improving GPU utilization for multi-tenant LLM serving.

tracking_records.title: From Local Mismatch to Global Impact: Optimizing Cache Reuse Policy for Efficient Diffusion
tracking_records.topic: diffusion cache policy / video-image generation acceleration
tracking_records.why: Diffusion models have achieved dominant performance in visual generation but suffer from substantial inference overhead. While cache-based acceleration has emerged as a promising solution, existing policies rely on local similarity heuristics, which we identify as being significantly misaligned with final generation quality. This discrepancy stems from the non-uniform propagation and accumulation of errors along the denoising trajectory. To address this, we propose Global-Impact Cache (GCache). We first establish a rigorous theoretical characterization of the error propagation upper bound. Recognizing that this bound can be overly conservative for complex, highly non-convex diffusion models, we further reparameterize the propagation exponent with a Bernstein form and reformulate cache policy search as a bilevel optimization problem. In detail, GCache identifies an optimal reuse policy in the inner objective while aligning the error-weighting function with generation quality loss in the outer objective. This framework effectively reconciles theoretical rigor with empirical performance, learning to prioritize computation where it most impacts visual fidelity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GCache consistently outperforms prior caching strategies on both video and image generation. Notably, on the state-of-the-art Wan2.1 video diffusion model, GCache maintains a 2.17x speedup while significantly enhancing generation quality, reducing LPIPS from 0.1095 to 0.0316.

tracking_records.title: From LLM Inference to Agentic Workloads: Characterization and Implications for Serving Systems
tracking_records.why: Agentic applications are shifting AI serving from isolated model inference to long-running workloads in which LLMs coordinate tools, environments, and persistent state. However, the system behavior of these workloads---where latency, cost, and bottlenecks arise---remains poorly characterized, leaving serving systems to rely on assumptions built for conventional inference. We present AgentSysBench, a benchmark suite and measurement toolkit with ten representative agentic applications and unified systems-level instrumentation. Across controlled deployments and production traces, we identify six properties that distinguish agentic workloads from conventional LLM serving: (1) execution is heavyweight and stateful, with non-LLM components dominating latency in 5 of 10 applications and sandbox working-set memory peaking at 28 GB per session; (2) applications compose components with heterogeneous resource affinity---GPU-bound inference, memory-bound retrieval, CPU-bound sandboxes---whose task latencies diverge by up to 32x; (3) bottlenecks shift across requests, models, and deployments; (4) production sessions hold state idle for minutes to hours between active steps; (5) a control-plane tax---auxiliary LLM calls and context overhead from tool schemas and observations---crowds out productive compute and context; and (6) production traces from three applications reveal heavy cross-request redundancy in search queries and web fetches, exposing a large caching opportunity. Four design explorations demonstrate that these findings are actionable: task-aware serving reduces latency by 29--40%, communication-aware placement by up to 4.5x, state offloading reduces memory usage by 4.6x, and tool-result caching removes 35.2% of redundant search calls and saves 19.3% of aggregate search latency.

tracking_records.title: Every Expert Counts: ExactMoE for Memory-Efficient W4A16 Inference
tracking_records.topic: MoE memory-efficient W4A16 inference / GPU slot cache
tracking_records.why: Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models reduce arithmetic by activating only a small subset of experts per token, yet deployment still requires storing and moving the full expert bank. We present ExactMoE, an inference design that applies symmetric group-128 four-bit weight quantization only to routed experts, stores those experts in kernel-native MARLIN form in pinned host memory, and executes all selected experts through a configurable GPU-resident slot cache and fused grouped MoE kernels. The router, attention, embeddings, normalization layers, and language-model head remain in BF16. "Exact" refers to complete expert availability and an unchanged top-k routing procedure: no expert is pruned, substituted, or forced to execute on the CPU. It does not imply numerical identity with the BF16 model. On OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct, evaluated on a single NVIDIA L4, a 16-slot configuration reduces peak reserved GPU memory from 14.168 to 1.836 GiB (87.04%) while retaining 81.85% of BF16 decode throughput. A fully resident 64-slot configuration reaches 31.923 tokens/s versus 21.662 tokens/s for BF16 while reserving 4.061 GiB. Across 12,450 zero-shot multiple-choice questions, ExactMoE obtains 70.3534% normalized accuracy versus 70.8996% for BF16, retaining 99.23% of the baseline accuracy. In a matched 16-token ablation, fused grouped execution is 1.97x as fast as a sequential W4 reference. These results identify a practical memory-transfer-throughput frontier for complete-expert MoE inference.

tracking_records.title: EcoVLA: Energy-Efficient Device-Edge Co-Inference for Vision-Language-Action Models under Real-Time Constraints
tracking_records.why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising foundation for Embodied AI, but their high inference cost poses significant challenges for deployment in robotic systems. In practice, on-device inference is constrained by limited compute capacity and energy budgets, struggling to simultaneously satisfy real-time control and energy efficiency requirements. Alternatively, offloading the inference workload to an edge server is susceptible to fluctuations in system conditions, introducing unpredictable latency risks. Device-edge co-inference offers a promising solution, but systematic research tailored to VLA models remains scarce, particularly a unified co-inference framework that jointly addresses real-time constraints and system-level energy efficiency. Thus, we propose EcoVLA, an adaptive device-edge co-inference framework for VLA models that maximizes system energy efficiency under real-time constraints. EcoVLA first introduces a unified stage-level abstraction over different VLA paradigms, establishing an architecture-agnostic co-inference design space. It then formulates a joint device-edge-network latency and energy prediction model to enable rapid runtime evaluation of candidate co-inference schemes. Building on this, EcoVLA continuously selects the energy-optimal scheme satisfying real-time constraints with millisecond-level overhead, adapting to runtime variations in network and system states. Furthermore, EcoVLA incorporates a lightweight transmission mechanism for inter-stage intermediate tensors to reduce the communication overhead incurred by cross-device collaboration. Experimental results across VLA models show that EcoVLA improves system energy efficiency by up to 236% over existing co-inference approaches under a 20 Hz action output frequency constraint, while consistently maintaining SLO satisfaction under dynamic network and edge workload conditions.

tracking_records.title: DeaMoE: Efficient MoE Structure for Fast Small-Batch Decoding
tracking_records.why: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have been widely adopted in real-time interactive applications such as coding assistants, real-time audio-video interaction systems. To meet the extremely low response latency requirements of these scenarios, practitioners commonly employ small-batch decoding, under which MoE inference becomes memory-bound and is severely bottlenecked by expert weight loading. However, this bottleneck has received limited attention, and existing solutions such as post-training weight compression or fine-grained expert design during pre-training either degrade model accuracy or introduce additional computation and communication overhead. To tackle this issue, we propose DeaMoE, a decoding-efficient MoE architecture, in which the experts are grouped into several departments, and the experts belonging to the same department share most parameters since they come from the same professional field, and additionally each expert contains a few private parameters to reflect its uniqueness. Moreover, we design customized two-stage routing strategy for DeaMoE to avoid redundant loading, under which DeaMoE greatly improves the efficiency during LLM decoding. Compared with vanilla MoE, DeaMoE reduces per-step loaded weights by up to 50.9% and achieves up to 1.33 end-to-end TPOT speedup for the pre-trained 7B model on A40, and up to 2.00x and 1.97x peak speedup for DeepSeek-V3 on A40 and H100 in microbenchmarks.

tracking_records.title: Beyond Capacity: Scalable MoE LLM Inference via High-Bandwidth Flash with Direct GPU and HBM Paths
tracking_records.why: Modern mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models increasingly strain the capacity and cost efficiency of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), as rapidly growing expert weights must be provisioned close to GPUs. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) offers substantially greater capacity, but conventional designs typically deliver HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through HBM, leaving an additional direct GPU-HBF connection underutilized. We explore an HBF organization that simultaneously exploits two independent expert-delivery routes: a direct path that transfers expert weights from HBF to the GPU and a relay path that transfers them from HBF through the HBM base die to the GPU. Whole experts are assigned to one of the two routes, and transfers over both routes proceed concurrently, increasing aggregate expert-delivery bandwidth without replicating expert weights or introducing a shared relay bottleneck. Early expert determination identifies upcoming experts ahead of their conventional execution point, allowing HBF read latency to overlap with preceding computation, while separate management of immutable expert weights and mutable KV-cache data reduces interference between the two traffic classes. We evaluate the architecture using an event-driven continuous-batching LLM serving simulator with empirically measured GPU compute latencies. Across representative MoE workloads, concurrently utilizing the direct GPU-HBF and HBF-HBM-GPU routes consistently improves expert-delivery efficiency over designs restricted to either route alone. For a representative workload, the proposed architecture can achieve 1.94$\times$ higher throughput and 1.90$\times$ end-to-end speedup over a design that delivers all HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through the HBM base die.

tracking_records.why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in the field of embodied AI, but their high computational cost and limited predicted action length hinder real-time deployment. Although Dadu-Corki, a dedicated accelerator for efficient embodied AI, has been introduced, it does not exploit the inherent interaction patterns between the robot and its environment, which results in a relatively short predicted action length. We observe that robotic environments naturally alternate between active states-where precise actions are crucial-and inactive states-where actions have limited impact on task success. This insight enables a new scheduling opportunity: long-action-length speculative prediction in inactive states, paired with selective verification in active states. We propose SpecVLA, an algorithm-system co-design framework that adaptively balances action length, inference latency, and task reliability. On the algorithm side, SpecVLA introduces a state-aware VLA inference execution paradigm and a hardware-friendly construction of a smaller verification model (sVLA) using differential residuals and block-wise mixed-precision quantization. On the system side, we develop a heterogeneous architecture consisting of a GPU and a robotic-specific hardware module, along with a speculative dataflow that decouples VLA and sVLA through parallel execution. Comprehensive evaluations on OpenVLA and RDT across LIBERO and ManiSkill benchmarks show that SpecVLA reduces end-to-end latency significantly while preserving task success rate. By enabling long-action-length speculative prediction with timely verification, SpecVLA achieves real-time robotic manipulation with both high efficiency and reliability.

tracking_records.title: 3L-D: A Low-Light Level Dataset from a Sensor-Agnostic, Alignment-Preserving Acquisition Framework
tracking_records.why: 该工作提供跨可见光与近红外的低照度图像/视频数据集，并比较代表性深度学习基线在重建质量、感知质量和推理延迟上的权衡。主要贡献是数据采集与对齐框架而非模型效率优化，因此仅作为低照度视觉效率评测的低优先级数据资源。

tracking_records.title: 3D-BBDA: Backpropagation-Free Black-Box Domain Adaptation for Robust 3D Point Cloud Recognition
tracking_records.why: Official abstract proposes backpropagation-free black-box domain adaptation with prototype alignment for 3D point-cloud recognition. Relevant to adaptation cost and robotics perception, but the abstract does not establish serving/latency or accelerator-efficiency results.

tracking_records.title: $TF^2$-Steering: Action Refinement with Tactile Forecasts and Feedback via Velocity-Field Steering
tracking_records.why: The official arXiv abstract describes a tactile MoE that steers a flow-matching action expert across simulated and real manipulation tasks. It belongs to the protected action-head/flow Physical-AI neighborhood, but no inference-efficiency, serving, memory, compute, or acceleration improvement is reported. Retain as P2 metadata only; do not claim an Efficient-ML acceleration contribution or request a PDF.
